description:
Returns the full spec payload for a provider + capability, including canonical_example.ts source code.
Use this to get the complete integration guide — auth pattern, endpoint, schemas, gotchas, and a TypeScript example — before writing API calls.

The response includes a "status" field:
  - "verified": tested against the provider's API, in "sandbox" or "production" (verified_in / verification.environment)
  - "deprecated": the provider is retiring it — "deprecation" gives the reason, replaced_by (the capability to use instead) and removed_after
  - anything else (e.g. "ready", "unverified"): written from the provider's documentation, NOT tested against the live API
"verification" says how and when it was tested; sandbox proves the request and response shapes, not production behaviour.
"open_questions", when present, lists what the provider's docs do not answer: tell the user before relying on the spec.
"environments", when present, gives each documented environment's base URL; a missing one is undocumented — ask the user, never guess.
"auth.credentials" / "signing" / "token_exchange" / "apply" and "webhook.signature", when present, describe the auth and webhook signature steps exactly: follow them.
"parameters", when present, lists the path, query and header parameters; "input_schema" is the request body only. A path parameter fills the {name} placeholder of endpoint.url.
"success_condition", when present, names the response field (dotted path) that says the call succeeded: a 2xx response with another value is a failure.

If status is not "verified", always warn the user before generating integration code: "This spec has not been tested against the live API yet and may contain errors."

Args:
  - provider (string): Provider slug e.g. "paycard"
  - capability (string): Capability name e.g. "create_payment"
  - variant (string[]?): Discriminator values to keep, e.g. ["mobile_money_ghs"] or ["bank", "NGN"].
    In every union (oneOf) of input_schema and response_schema, only the branches pinned to one of
    these values are kept; a union none of them matches is left whole. Without it, all branches are
    returned. The response lists every value under "variants" (discriminator property → values).
    A large spec also carries "_mcp_size_note": if your client cut the result, call again with the
    variant you need.

Returns: Full Spec object with canonical_example string (plus _mcp_warning when status is not
"verified"). If not found: isError, with { error, available_capabilities } when the provider exists
— capability names are each provider's own, pick one from that list — and did_you_mean (closest
provider slugs or capability names) when one is close. A capability removed from the registry
after a provider deprecation answers isError with removed_in, reason and alternatives.
Use search_specs or list_providers first to discover available providers and capabilities.

variant.description: Discriminator values to keep, e.g. ["mobile_money_ghs"] — see "variants" in search_specs
